sentences.text:
The petitioners have filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR- 37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021 in respect of Sy. No.9/1C measuring to an extent of 860.80 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.

.2. The definite case of the petitioners is that the property bearing Sy. No.9/1C measuring to an extent of 860.80 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.16,58,761/- as compensation for 860.80 Sq. feet of the land belongs to the petitioners.

The petitioners received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of A.P.
No.81/2022 Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 18.05.2012.

Accordingly, the said application taken by Krishnappa J M Since Dead By Lrs ... vs The Project Director And General ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178978152/
2 the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3.

sentences.text: In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contentions urged by the petitioners are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioners have not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioners cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioners is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-23,
22, 21, 20, 19, 18, 17, 49, 26, 24/2011-12, 37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioners filed this petition under Section A.P. No.81/2022 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioners claim that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on records and in violation of Principles of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.
The petitioners claim that the respondent No.3 committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioners for deciding the market value.
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No. 3 has not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The award dated 28.01.2011 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidance value under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for prime land of the petitioner.
The land acquired is more than value than the award amount, even the amount awarded.
The respondent No. A.P. No.81/2022 3 enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed before the Court, which is against probabilities of the case.

That due to land acquired by the respondents, the petitioner lost his land and the adjacent land owners of the same village have got a high value for their property, hence, this Court has to reconsider the claim of the petitioner.
The respondent No. 3 grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated midst of the lands commercially developed.

The LAO and Arbitrator has not recorded any evidence and not considered for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market value along with interest from the date of taking possession till the date of payment.
Accordingly, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

The respondent No.1 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the Krishnappa J M Since Dead By Lrs ... vs The Project Director And General ...

The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioners in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioners by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to him and when he approached the concerned authority on 17.12.2021, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.
Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9. The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.
The respondent No.3 has not appeared before the Court and hence, he has been placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-23, 22, 21, 20, 19, 18, 17, 49, 26, 24/2011-12, 37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021 secured from the Arbitrator.

.11. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
A.P. No.81/2022 1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioners is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.12. Heard the arguments.

The learned advocate for the petitioners relied on judgments reported in (1) In Civil Appeal No. 7064/2019 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 9599 of 2019) - Union of India Vs.
Tarsem Singh; (2) In No. SLP (C) No.19775/2021 (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 584) ; (3) SLAO and another Vs. Sri. Muthaiah and another in MFA No. 2930/2020; (4) D.S. Gopala Krishna Vs. The Project Director and General Manager and others in A.P. No.15045/2022, (5) NHAI and another Vs. The Additional Commissioner and others in A.A. No.03/2022 and (6) In Suo Motu Writ petition (Civil)
No. 3 of 2020 with respect to Cognizance for Extension of Limitation extending the limitation period of 90 days A.P. No.81/2022 from 01.03.2022.

4 Points No.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .13. POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioners have made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.14. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioners are the owners of the property bearing Sy. No.9/1C measuring to an extent of 860.80 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka and the said property A.P. No.81/2022 has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010 for the purpose of widening of NH-7
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,927/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.16,58,761/- being the land value was disbursed to the petitioners as compensation.

.15. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioners filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that they are entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 18.05.2012.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/CR-37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021.

The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at A.P. No.81/2022 Rs.5,250/- per Sq.
feet from Rs.1,927/- per Sq.feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs.3,323/- per Sq. feet.
.16.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioners in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioners is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioners and also without considering the claim of the petitioners that other properties have enhanced the market value which is much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No. 3.
The said claim of the petitioners is also found in the award.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No. 3, it is clear that the respondent No. 3 considering the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide notification bearing No. CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation, but there is no material on record to show that the petitioners have produced the alleged documents claimed by the A.P. No.81/2022 petitioners in the petition for perusal of Arbitrator/respondent No. 3.
.17.

However, it is the definite case of petitioners that the Arbitrator has enhanced the meager amount though the value of the property is much higher than awarded / enhanced by the Arbitrator / respondent No.3.

Hence, it is to be considered that whether the enhancement made by the respondent No. 3 / Arbitrator is meager or substantial.
.18.

On perusal of the award passed by the respondent No.3 shows that the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation from Rs. 1,927/- per Sq. feet to Rs. 5,250/- per Sq. feet i.e., almost 3 times than the Krishnappa J M Since Dead By Lrs ... vs The Project Director And General ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178978152/
5 market value determined by the LAO.

entities.text: Krishnappa J M Since Dead By Lrs ... vs The Project Director And General
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the said enhancement by the LAO cannot be considered that the enhancement is only meager enhancement.
Of course the Arbitrator in some cases enhanced the compensation 3 times and if that is accepted, the Arbitrator ought to have enhanced the compensation at Rs. 5,781/- per Sq. feet.

Therefore, certainly the A.P. No.81/2022 Arbitrator has awarded almost Rs. 500/- less per Sq. feet considered to the other awards in-respect of the land of same village acquired under the same notification bearing No. SO No.3159 (E) dated 09.12.2009 and final notification dated SO No. 1874(E) dated 30.07.2010.
.19.
In support of this contention, the petitioners have produced the copy of the order passed in LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021.
In the said case, the LAO has enhanced the compensation 3 times of the compensation awarded by LAO/ respondent No. 2.
Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,927/- per Sq. feet and it is enhanced to the tune of Rs.5,250/- per Sq. feet by enhancing only Rs.3,323/- per Sq. feet.
Therefore, the claim of the petitioners is probable that the respondent No.3 has not properly appreciated the material placed before him while passing the order.
Apart from that, the impugned order of the respondent No. 3 also does not disclose any reasons for the A.P. No.81/2022 enhancement made in the impugned award.
The Arbitrator has stated much about contention taken by petitioners and respondent No. 1 in the order and abruptly decided the market value without assigning any proper reasons.

Hence,
the order of the LAO certainly liable to be intervened by this court.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.20. Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioners to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

C o n s e q u e n t l y , t h e i m p u g n e d a w a r d p a s s e d b y t h e r e s p o n d e n t N o . 3 i n c a s e LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021 in respect of Sy. No.9/1C measuring to an extent of 860.80 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka A.P. No.81/2022 Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka is set aside with liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court records.
